cards.name: Press-photo frame with caption strip
cards.summary: A news photo sits in a clean white border with a soft shadow, and a dark strip under it carries the caption and the photo credit.
avoid: cropping or retouching the photo's content to fit the frame: crop only, never alter what it shows
a caption strip over the picture's key area: put it below the image, or over a quiet edge
dropping the credit: the strip is where the source and photographer go

cards.name: Quote card with speaker cut-out
cards.summary: A speaker is cut out of their photo and set on a tinted, softened background with a thin white outline, next to their quote in large type with the name and date.
use_for: quote cards for interviews, talks and statements
explainer slides that attribute a claim
avoid: putting words in someone's mouth: use the exact quote, the date and the source
text over the face: keep the quote beside the cut-out, never across it
a hard white outline on a rough automatic cut-out: refine the mask edge first or the outline shows every flaw

steps.note: Setup (script): a dark blue rectangle over the backdrop.
Uniform transparency 30 on the dark rectangle (about 70 percent opaque) for contrast.

Cut-out: a 62-point polygon that follows the silhouette of the left subject (its outline down to the picture's lower edge); the points were measured against the photo offline, because CorelDRAW has no automatic subject selection (a real job draws the path with the Pen or Bezier tool, or traces a mask); the original photo is placed inside it (AddToPowerClip) above the backdrop, and a white copy of the polygon goes behind it for the outline.
Contour outside on the white copy: one white step, 0.09 in (about 9 px at 1920: thin, as the recipe says, but a clear white line), round corners.
Soft dark drop shadow under the outlined cut-out: 45 percent, feather 10, so it separates from the blurred backdrop.

steps.script:
LEFT, MAXW = 10.4, 8.7
lines = [("Exact quote goes here,", "#FFFFFF", 54, 8.6), ("word for word,", "#FFFFFF", 54, 7.5), ("in large type.", "#FFD400", 54, 6.4)]
for text, col, size, y in lines:
    q = layer.CreateArtisticText(0.0, 0.0, text, 0, -1, "Arial Black", size)
    q.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb(col))
    q.Outline.SetNoOutline()
    if q.SizeWidth > MAXW:
        k = MAXW / q.SizeWidth
        q.SetSize(q.SizeWidth * k, q.SizeHeight * k)
    q.SetPosition(LEFT, y)
q4 = layer.CreateArtisticText(0.0, 0.0, "Speaker name, role  |  date", 0, -1, "Arial", 24)
q4.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#C9D3E3"))
q4.Outline.SetNoOutline()
q4.SetPosition(LEFT, 4.4)
result = q4

cards.name: Breaking-news strap
cards.summary: A bold lower-third bar: a saturated colour band with a slight gradient and shadow, a contrasting label box at the left and the headline in white.
use_for: lower thirds and chyrons for video explainers
avoid: using 'breaking' styling for old or routine news: label it 'update' or 'explainer'
more than one line of text in the strap: it stops reading at a glance
low-contrast colour pairs: white on saturated red or deep blue, never on yellow

steps.note: Layer > New Fill Layer > Solid Color for the bar (script): a full-width rectangle selection 0, 690 to 1920, 810 px (lower third, 120 px tall), a solid #C8102E fill layer with that selection as its mask, then Deselect. Ran; labelled 'bar'.

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Layer Style > Drop Shadow: 45 % black Multiply, 4 px at 90 degrees, Size 10. Set without error; the shadow under the bar is faint over the photo.

steps.note: One layer style: both effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style). Applied without error.
Second Solid Color fill layer for the label box (script): rectangle 60, 665 to 440, 835 px, solid #FFFFFF, standing a little taller than the bar at its left end, then Deselect. Ran; labelled 'label'.

Edit > Transform > Skew on the label box (script; target 'label'): horizontal skew -8 degrees about its centre, via the transform action. Ran; the run shows a slanted parallelogram. The selection was cleared first so the whole layer is transformed.

cards.name: Key-number highlight
cards.summary: The one number that matters is pulled out: big type with a coloured glow or keyline, sitting on a hand-drawn highlighter mark.
use_for: chart call-outs (the latest value, the record)
avoid: highlighting a number without its unit, date and source
glow on light backgrounds: use the keyline or the marker there
several highlighted numbers on one card: highlight one, keep the rest plain

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: Layer Style > Stroke on the number's type layer (target 'type'): Outside 4 px #111111. The run shows a thin dark keyline round the white figures.

effects.name: Outer Glow
effects.note: Layer Style > Outer Glow: Screen, #FFD400, 85 %, Spread 10, Size 28. The run shows a thin pale yellow halo round the figures (it sits on the yellow marker, so it is subtle there). Screen can only lighten, so it would not show on a white card; there use the keyline and the marker.

steps.note: One layer style: both effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style). Input: 380 px Arial Black white '42%' on a pale cool grey card (#DDE2EA; the first run's mid-grey card turned the marker a dull mustard), a placeholder number: state the unit, period and source beside the real one (manual).

Marker: Layer > New Fill Layer > Solid Color (script), made with the background layer active so it lands below the type: a hand-drawn-looking selection (a polygon, about 1060 x 300 px, whose top and bottom edges waver by a few pixels and whose ends are slanted and slightly bowed), a solid #FFEE19 fill layer with that selection as mask, then Deselect and a -3 degree rotation about its centre. Ran; the run shows a slightly tilted yellow band with wavering, uneven edges rather than a clean rectangle. It is a polygon, not a brush stroke, so it has no pen texture or overprint darkening, and the jagged edge reads more as a rough cut than a pen mark.

Marker layer set to Multiply (it is the active layer): ran. The run shows the band multiplying with the pale grey card to a vivid yellow (about RGB 221 / 211 / 23 against the card's 221 / 226 / 234), as a highlighter pen would, with the white figures on top (the first run's mid-grey card and #FFE14D gave a dull mustard).

cards.name: Map highlight callout
cards.summary: One region of a map is lifted out: the rest goes grey and darker, the region keeps its colour with a bright outline and glow, and a label box points to it.
use_for: locating a place in a news explainer
regional data maps (one region in focus)
avoid: map sources you have no right to use: draw from an open-licence map and credit it
disputed borders without a note: say which boundary source the map follows
glow on the region over a busy satellite image: use the outline only

steps.note: Script (new first step, target 'background'): a stylised stand-in base map on a blank page, a pale blue ground and seven flat-coloured polygons drawn with selection.select and fill. It is not a real map: use an open-licence map and credit its source (manual). Ran; everything is pixels on the one background layer.

Layer > New > Layer Via Copy (script, target 'background'): select the region's outline polygon (1000, 330 to 1560, 740 px), copyToLayer, then Deselect. Ran; the region is its own layer ('Layer 1', labelled 'region').

cards.name: Privacy blur or pixelation

use_for: protecting bystanders, minors and private individuals in news photos
avoid: light blur or small mosaic cells: faces and text can be recovered; use cells at least a quarter of the face width
live, reversible effects in the delivered file (smart filters, Illustrator effects, CorelDRAW lenses): flatten or rasterise before export
forgetting the metadata: strip location and camera data on export
